technocore.head_message:
fix(humans): align the message input limit with the server (#142)

The message box on `/humans` stops accepting input at 2000 characters.
The server takes 4096.

What made me file this rather than shrug at it is that the page
disagrees with itself. The WebMCP `say` tool that same page publishes
declares `maxLength: 4096` for `text`, and both it and the input box
post to `POST /r/<room>`. One page, one operation, two limits, and the
smaller one is the one a person hits.

`maxlength` is also silent when it bites. There is no message and no
counter. The input just stops taking characters, so someone pasting a
long message loses the tail without being told it happened or how much
went missing.

### Checked against a running instance

```
CHAT_ROOT=./data uv run uvicorn --app-dir src app:app --port 8080

POST /r/probe  {"text": 4096 chars}   200, stored 4096, nothing truncated
POST /r/probe  {"text": 4097 chars}   400 text too long: 4097 characters, and the limit is 4096
```

So 4096 is real on the lane the page actually uses, not just the number
in `store.MAX_TEXT_CHARS`.

### The change

One attribute, 2000 to 4096.

The test reads `maxlength` off the page as served and checks it against
`store.clean_text`, which is the validator that lane reaches. That
mirrors `test_humans_name_inputs_match_the_server_name_limit` directly
above it, which does the same thing for `#room` and `#nick` against
`valid_name`. Putting it in the same file keeps one place that answers
"do the boxes on this page agree with the server".

It fails without the fix: at 2000, `clean_text("a" * 2001)` raises
nothing, so the `pytest.raises` block reports `DID NOT RAISE
StoreError`.

### Gates

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty check` all clean. `coverage
report` 97.40%. `sz.py --check` ok, and the core baseline does not move
since `humans.html` is not core and the test is not either.

One note in the interest of not overclaiming: on one full-suite run I
saw `test_the_post_lanes_do_not_block_the_event_loop` fail. It did not
reproduce in three further full runs or six isolated ones, and `main`
was clean across five runs on the same machine. It asserts a 0.2s
ceiling on event loop scheduling gaps, and I was running under Docker on
Windows with coverage on, so I believe it was host noise rather than
anything here. Mentioning it because 1 in 4 is not 0 in 4.

---

I used Claude to help investigate this. The verification against the
running service, and the writing, are mine.

Co-authored-by: faakhiranadiaz <304199974+faakhiranadiaz@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Sergey Vidyuk <svidyuk@gmail.com>

tclk.head_message:
feat(flop): add configurable HTLC settlement rail (#210)

## What

Add `@flop-labs/tclk-flop` with HTLC lock, verify, claim and refund.
Devnet is the default; testnet/mainnet require explicit RPC and genesis
pins. Signing remains local.

After recovery journaling, the rail rechecks the claim window and anchor
freshness before submitting, so a slow journal cannot knowingly deposit
into a stale deal.

## Why

tclk needs a value-bearing settlement rail. The optional package keeps
networking outside the protocol core. SPEC.md describes the actual
block-deadline and Ed25519 account bindings.

Hostile references cannot substitute chain, parties, amount or terms. A
bare HTLC does not prove work delivery; chain stalls can delay refunds.

## Devnet verification

Both paths finalized for **0.001 test FLOP**, with balance events and
`ExtrinsicSuccess`:

- Claim:
`0x634b4d1ca17876f08f805d7cb1f5a79667b2de86be44d9819abaec6d08408c03`
- Refund:
`0x574a55ac8578514c3c22605d6fb1d9af67c2fa7b7ca351563404b1049740354c`

[Receipts, reproduction and review regression
coverage](https://github.com/flop-labs/tclk/blob/795ff20e21cacce43e4ea146b2d88af7eba4268a/flop/VERIFICATION.md).
All four test escrows closed.

## Checks

- [x] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- [x] `pnpm -r --include-workspace-root build`
- [x] `pnpm -r --include-workspace-root test`: **249 passed**, including
72 rail tests.
- [x] Protocol drift and whitespace checks; golden vectors untouched.
- [x] Affected documentation and `CHANGELOG.md` updated.

sonnet.head_message:
Results: sonnet-2 — the winner, every allocation and DID, and how to check them (#86)

The permanent record of the sonnet-2 result: every allocation and every
DID, with what each is owed and the signed record that earned it.

- **Winner:** maragung-flop, chosen by FLOP Labs' judges from the
finalists quire, pom-team and maragung-flop.
- **Allocations:** 12,500 FLOP to each of 4 contributors; 7 FLOP to each
of 6,852 voters whose final ballot chose the winner; 2,036 FLOP rounding
remainder kept by FLOP Labs. 6,856 DIDs, 97,964 FLOP.
- **Verifiable:** `payouts.json` hashes to `ebc0de59…`, the
`payments_sha256` in the signed settle receipt at `d-sonnet-2-results`
seq 45498. `allocations.csv` and `payouts.json` agree DID for DID; every
file's hash is in `manifest.json`.

Everything here is built from the closed referee ledger and was
cross-checked against it: all 6,856 paid DIDs match the ledger's payout,
every contributor supplied accepted words, and every voter's counted
ballot is their own accepted record for the winner.

Adds `results/sonnet-2/` only. The pinned package and its
`manifest.json` are untouched; the package tests pass.
